title: Add temporal-spectral corridor canary and rate-tether rollout guard
author: Leah Kim
description: Context: We observed intermittent medium-duration latency glide events during cross-tenant traffic bursts that are not captured by point-in-time percentile detectors. Motivation: Introduce a canary evaluator that fuses temporal frequency information (spectral energy across short windows) with cohort-aligned latency corridors to detect gradual but meaningful regressions and noisy phase shifts. This PR implements the temporal-spectral corridor canary and a companion rate-tether rollout guard. Design summary: 1) Temporal-spectral canary computes short-time Fourier-like energy features on latency time series from synthetic probes and live traffic cohorts, normalizes by baseline spectral envelope, and tracks corridor breach probability via an exponentially-weighted hazard estimator. 2) Rate-tether guard ties allowed rollout velocity to observed throughput delta and corridor breach score; if the corridor breach probability crosses the high threshold the guard clamps traffic ramping to a conservative rate and triggers probe amplification. 3) Cohort stitching ensures per-tenant baselines are maintained; cohorts with low signal are pooled using a weighted reservoir to preserve sensitivity while avoiding noisy false positives. Implementation highlights: Added service/canary/temporal_spectral.py implementing the evaluator and a light-weight C extension wrapper for the tight spectral window filter; introduced tests in tests/canary/test_temporal_spectral.py; added runtime config knobs in infra/helm/canary-values.yaml; exposed metrics via observability/metrics.yaml (spectral_energy, corridor_breach_prob, rate_tether_state) and documented the approach in docs/perf/canaries.md. Rollout plan: start gated canary in eu-west-1 with 0.5% traffic shadow and synthetic probe amplification x4 for 24h, then staged ramp with rate-tether enabled at 2%/hour increments if corridor_breach_prob stays <0.05. Monitoring and alerts: new alerts added for corridor_breach_prob>0.2 sustained 10m, probe amplification failures, and rate-tether clamp events. Testing: unit tests and synthetic replay harness added; ran a 12h perf canary against prod-like traffic and verified no false positives and correct clamp behavior under injected drift. Backwards compatibility and safety: the guard is opt-in via feature flag; defaults to off for all Dedicated/private installs. Related work: follows ENG-4061 (cohort-based probe stitching) and ENG-4120 (rollout velocity controls).
